govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Pistols_Pistols: This FBI memorandum from SA Jack A. French is a Bureau file. The declassified memo is a primary source. Agents filed reports by the thousand. The memo may hold a clue. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the government archive.
half-a-dozen-girls: Anna Chapin Ray's cheerful story follows six schoolgirl friends through lessons, quarrels, secrets, and good times. Each girl has her own personality and troubles, and their friendship carries them through the small dramas of growing up. Written in the 1890s for young readers, it captures the warmth and mischief of girlhood with affection and humor.
betty-wales-sophomore-a-story-for-girls: Edith Kellogg Dunton continues the adventures of Betty Wales at Harding College in this second volume of the popular series. Now a sophomore, Betty navigates friendships, school spirit, and growing up with her usual warmth and good sense. The book captures college girl life of the early 1900s with affectionate, wholesome charm.
general-history-for-colleges-and-high-sc: P. V. N. Myers's comprehensive textbook carried students from ancient times to the modern age in one solid volume. Clear maps, timelines, and narratives made it a classroom standard for decades. Though scholarship has advanced, the book remains an interesting monument to how history was once taught.
esther-a-book-for-girls: Rosa Nouchette Carey — one of Victorian England's most popular writers for girls — tells Esther's story of growing up, with its friendships, faith, and first sorrows. Her heroines face life's trials with courage and goodness. Generations of young readers found comfort and guidance in Carey's gentle, moral tales.
while-the-billy-boils: Henry Lawson's classic collection gathers his bush stories — swagmen, shearers, and battlers around the campfire while the billy boils. His laconic humor and deep humanity made these tales Australia's own. The book that defined a nation's literature. Drovers, shearers, and swaggies yarn around outback fires in stories the world now calls classic.
familiar-spanish-travels: William Dean Howells takes his readers on familiar Spanish travels — through a Spain he knew and loved, from Madrid to Andalusia — with his usual gentle observation. His American eye finds the old country both charming and strange. Delightful wandering with a master of the quiet art.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acquaviva-car: A 1913 entry on the Acquaviva cardinals — the great Neapolitan family in the Sacred College. Thomas Shahan names their line. Claudio, the Jesuit general, was their brightest star. A family's century of red hats. Their palace hosted poets and painters. Naples remembers their splendid age.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-vessels: This 1913 reference piece on altar vessels — chalice, paten, and ciborium. Augustin Schulte details their consecration. Gold and silver serve the Blood. Bishops anoint them with chrism. The Mass's sacred instruments. Their touch is priests' alone. Their hallmarks prove the sterling silver.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-angels: A 1913 entry on angels — the Church's doctrine of the heavenly host. Hugh Pope sets out their nature and work. Nine choirs sing the endless praise. Guardians watch each soul. The fullest Catholic account. Their feast crowns September's end. Their names fill the litany's roll.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolic-sch: This 1913 reference piece on apostolic schools — the nurseries of young priests. Patrick Boyle describes their work. Small seminaries train the boys. The Church plants for the harvest. The seedbeds of the priesthood. Their pupils fill the great seminaries. Their discipline is strict and kindly.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-appeals: A 1913 entry on appeals in canon law — the recourse to the higher judge. Hector Papi sets out the just procedure. The Church guards the accused's right. Rome is the final court. The ladder of ecclesiastical justice. Their course is strictly regulated.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bath-and-well: A 1913 entry on Bath and Wells — the ancient English diocese. Edwin Burton traces its bishops. Its cathedral crowns the Mendips. The vicars' close keeps medieval time. A great see of the West Country. Its swans ring the palace bell. Its bishop's palace moat holds the swans.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bells: This 1913 reference article on bells — the Church's bronze voices. Herbert Thurston traces their blessed use. The tower calls the faithful to prayer. The passing bell tolls the dead. The music of the Christian day. Their blessing is the baptism of bronze.
